$doc: Pass/fail limits of node e2e/run-e2e.mjs (initial values; tighten as the engine matures). Resolution per run: default <- <meta.scene> (object | yard) <- datasets[<dataset name>]. Check names and their meaning: e2e/lib/e2e-checks.mjs (CHECKS). {min, max} bound the value; 'claims' require the result's MetricInfo to claim a property when the sensors it needs were passed (metric / gravityAligned: IMU or GPS; northAligned: compass or GPS). Checks of properties that are not claimed (scale, gravity, heading) and dense checks without a dense run are skipped. registrationRate is registered / images the engine tried (stats.images, else live keyframes). Yard dense limits are lower than object: with EXACT poses the dense stage reaches ~0.23-0.34 completeness at tau = 0.1 m on that 120 m scene (e2e/README.md, dense-gt reference run). The -real datasets (iPhone capture artefacts: rolling shutter, focus breathing, hand shake with fast pans, blur, JPEG 0.85; e2e/README 'Real-capture robustness') get dataset entries tighter than their scene's limits, so that the failure modes they were built for are caught: the pre-fix baselines fail them (yard-real: ATE 0.10, rotation 152 deg, gravity 3.5 deg, heading 7.8 deg; object-real: rotation 0.73 deg from a principal point 8 px off, IMU scale -4.3 %), the fixed pipeline passes with a ~2-6x margin (2026-10, CPU features, 480 px dense: yard-real ATE 3.1e-4, rotation 0.09 deg, focal +0.15 %, scale +1.6 %, gravity 0.06 deg, heading -0.9 deg, dense P/C 0.961/0.352 with accuracy p50 8.8 mm; object-real ATE 2.8e-4, rotation 0.08 deg, focal +0.08 %, scale -0.8 %, dense C 0.993 with accuracy p50 0.31 mm = 2.3e-4 of the extent, baseline 1.3 mm; the rotation-only rolling-shutter correction measured 3.1 mm and rotation 0.27 deg, which these limits also reject). object-real also carries the object-isolation acceptance of the automatic object box (src/dense/object-roi.ts; the values of its spec): box IoU with meta.focus >= 0.6, box contains meta.focus shrunk by 1 cm, mesh.ply vertices outside meta.focus +- 2 cm <= 5 %. They apply to mesh runs with the box on (skipped with --no-mesh or --no-object-roi, the unbounded baseline); offline on the 6 stored object-real sparse models the box scores IoU 0.73-0.77 and contains meta.focus - 1 cm (its y faces 8-12 mm beyond meta.focus), the mesh share is first measured by the central run.
